Her friend Sophie says: “You need help. Take screenshots of the messages!” Elif takes screenshots. Then she tells her parents everything.

Her parents are not angry. They say: “Thank you for telling us everything. We'll help you.” On Monday they go to the teacher together. The teacher talks to the boy. Elif feels better now.
questions: Where does Elif get the nasty messages?
What does Sophie say?
Who does Elif tell everything?

wrong: Delete the screenshots of the messages!

cyber-a12-09-hilfe-holen:1.text:
David is fifteen and likes playing online. One day a stranger writes to him: “Send me money, or I'll show your chats to everyone!” David is afraid. What should he do?

He calls a helpline. The counselling is free and anonymous. The woman on the phone says: “This is serious. Talk to your parents. Don't delete anything, because the messages are evidence.”

David talks to his father. Together they go to the police and file a report. The police officer says: “In an emergency, call the emergency number straight away.” David is glad: he got help.

gloss.erstatten: file (Anzeige erstatten — to file a report)

questions: What does the stranger want?
What is the counselling like?
Why shouldn't David delete anything?
Where do David and his father go?

translate.tr: The counselling is free and anonymous.
wrong: The counselling costs money and is anonymous.
The counselling is free but not anonymous.

translate.tr: David goes to the police with his father.
wrong: David goes to the police with his mother.
David doesn't go to the police with his father.
David calls the police with his father.

cyber-a12-10-gute-gewohnheiten:0.text:
Lukas goes to the HTL in Vienna. He is often online. His teacher says: “Good habits protect you.” She gives the class three rules.

First rule: be careful with links and messages. Think for a moment and don't click right away. Second rule: look after your phone. Never leave it lying around alone at school. Third rule: check your accounts and passwords regularly.

Lukas likes the rules. Now he does a small check every week. And after an hour at the computer he always takes a break.
questions: How many rules does the teacher give?
What should Lukas do with links?
What does Lukas do after an hour at the computer?

cyber-a12-10-gute-gewohnheiten:1.text:
Nina is sixteen. Her screen time is very long: five hours a day! On Saturday she wants to change something. Her cousin Paul studies at TU Wien. He has a few tips for her.

First Nina cleans up her phone. She deletes old apps and accounts. Then she covers the webcam on her laptop. Paul says: “An uncovered webcam is a danger.”

Nina asks: “And what if I make a mistake?” Paul laughs: “Everyone makes mistakes, that's normal. Just pay attention to small things, for example the padlock in the browser.” Nina thinks the tips are great.
questions: How long is Nina's screen time?
What does Nina do with the webcam?
Who is Paul?

translate.tr: An uncovered webcam is a danger.
wrong: A covered webcam is a danger.
An uncovered webcam is not a danger.
Everyone makes mistakes, that's not normal.

informatik-a12-computer:0.text:
Lea has a new computer. The screen is big and the keyboard is quiet. The mouse is small and black. Lea is very happy.

Today Lea is writing a text for school. She opens the program and writes for an hour. Then she saves the file. The file is called “Referat”. Lea also makes a folder. The folder is called “Schule”. She puts the file in the folder.

In the evening Lea looks for the file. Where is it? Lea opens the folder “Schule”. There is the file!

gloss.sie: she; they; (here also) it — about the file: die Datei

questions: What is the screen like?
What is the file called?
Where is the file in the evening?

wrong: Lea is buying a new computer.

informatik-a12-computer:1.text:
Tom studies computer science. In the morning he downloads an app onto his phone. The app is free. Then he reads his emails. One email is an advert. Tom deletes it immediately.

In the afternoon Tom wants to print a document. But the printer isn't printing. Tom presses every key. Nothing happens! He looks for a solution on the internet. A new program helps. Tom downloads the program, and now the printer works again.
questions: What does Tom do with the advert?
What is the problem in the afternoon?
What helps Tom?

informatik-a12-02-internet:0.text:
Jonas has homework: he is writing a report about the Danube. He opens the browser on his laptop. The Wi-Fi at home is very slow today. But finally Jonas is online.

He searches with a search engine. He types “Donau” and finds a lot of websites. The first website is just advertising. The second one is good, it has photos and a map.

Jonas clicks on a link and reads. His sister Mia says: “You've been surfing for two hours!” Jonas laughs: “I'm not surfing, I'm studying!”
questions: What is Jonas writing a report about?
What is the Wi-Fi like today?
What does the second website have?
What does Jonas say to Mia?

translate.tr: The first website is just advertising.
wrong: The second website is just advertising.
The first website is not advertising.
He is looking for a link.

informatik-a12-02-internet:1.text:
In the evening Jonas chats with his friend Elif. Elif is writing a report too. She asks: “Do you have good information?” Jonas sends her a link.

Jonas now has twelve tabs open. That's too many! He makes a bookmark for the best website. Then he closes the other tabs.

Elif searches herself too. She gets a thousand results, but only three are good. At ten o'clock Jonas goes offline. In the morning he has a message from Elif: “Thanks for the link!”
questions: Who does Jonas chat with?
What does Jonas do with the best website?
How many results are good for Elif?
When does Jonas go offline?

wrong: Jonas gets a link from her.

translate.tr: She gets a lot of results.
wrong: He gets a lot of results.
She is looking for a lot of results.

informatik-a12-03-smartphone:0.text:
Paul has a new smartphone. The display is big and the camera is great. Paul installs a lot of apps: games, music and a chat.

In the afternoon Paul is in town. He plays and chats for two hours. Then the battery is flat! Paul doesn't have a charger with him. He can't call his mother.

He goes into a café. The woman there helps him. Paul charges the phone for half an hour. Now the battery is half full. Paul says: “Tomorrow I'll take my charger with me!”
questions: What is great about the new smartphone?
Why can't Paul call his mother?
Where does Paul charge the phone?
How full is the battery at the end?

translate.tr: Paul doesn't have a charger with him.
wrong: Paul has a charger with him.
Paul doesn't have his phone with him.

informatik-a12-03-smartphone:1.text:
It's Sara's birthday on Saturday. Her grandma lives in Graz and can't come. In the evening Sara gets a call from Grandma: “Please send me photos!”

Sara's brother David photographs the party with his camera. He takes thirty photos. Sara swipes through the photos and taps the best ones. Then she looks for Grandma in her contacts and sends five photos.

On Sunday Sara goes to the cinema. There her phone is on silent. After the film she sees a message from Grandma: “The photos are wonderful!”
questions: Where does Sara's grandma live?
Who photographs the party?
How many photos does Sara send?
When does Sara see the message from Grandma?

translate.tr: Sara gets a call from Grandma.
wrong: Sara gets a message from Grandma.

translate.tr: At the cinema her phone is on silent.
wrong: At the cinema her phone is switched off.
At the cinema his phone is on silent.

informatik-a12-04-computerraum:0.text:
Today Nina has a lesson in the computer room for the first time. There are twenty places with computers. Nina looks for a place by the window. The room is dark, and Mr Huber, the teacher, switches on the light.

Nina wants to switch on the computer, but nothing happens. Mr Huber looks under the table. The plug isn't in the socket! Without electricity, of course, it doesn't work.

Now the computer works. The class works with a program for an hour. At the end Mr Huber says: “Please switch off the computers!”

gloss.mal: time (zum ersten Mal — for the first time)

questions: Where does Nina sit?
Why doesn't the computer work at first?
Who switches on the light?
How many places are there in the computer room?

translate.tr: Nina is looking for a place by the window.
wrong: Nina found a place by the window.
Nina is looking for a place by the door.

translate.tr: The plug isn't in the socket.
wrong: The plug is in the socket.
The cable isn't in the socket.
Please switch off the computer! (to one person)

informatik-a12-04-computerraum:1.text:
There are rules in the computer room. They hang on the door. Eating and drinking are not allowed, and your phone stays in your bag.

Nina logs in with her username and her password. She has her report on a USB stick. She opens the file and works until the break.

Then the bell rings. Nina quickly logs out. Mr Huber says: “Please tidy up your places!” Nina tidies up. But oh no, she forgets the USB stick in the computer! After the break she quickly fetches it.

gloss.meldet: meldet … an — logs in; meldet … ab — logs out

questions: Where do the rules hang?
What does Nina have on the USB stick?
What does Nina forget in the computer?

translate.tr: Eating and drinking are not allowed.
wrong: Eating is not allowed, but drinking is.
Please tidy up your place! (to one person)

informatik-a12-05-texte:0.text:
Jonas goes to school in Vienna. Today he is writing a text about his city. He opens a new document on the computer and types slowly.

The text has three paragraphs. In the first paragraph Jonas writes about the Prater. In the first line a letter is missing. The word isn't “Stat” but “Stadt”. Jonas corrects the word and reads the sentence again.

At the end the document has two pages. The teacher reads the text and says: “The text is good, but the word ‘super’ is in it too often!” Jonas laughs.

gloss.geht: goes; (in die Schule gehen) goes to school

questions: What does Jonas write about?
What is missing in the first line?
How many pages does the document have at the end?

translate.tr: Jonas types the text on the computer.
wrong: Jonas reads the text on the computer.
Jonas prints the text on the printer.

translate.tr: In the first line a letter is missing.
wrong: In the last line a letter is missing.
In the first line a word is missing.

informatik-a12-05-texte:1.text:
Mia and Elif are making a poster for the school party. Mia selects the title and makes it bold. Then she chooses a large font.

Elif copies a photo from the internet and pastes it in. But the photo is too big. Elif gets nervous and deletes the whole text. “Oh no!” she cries.

Mia laughs: “No problem. We'll undo it.” She presses Ctrl and Z. The text is back. Then Mia cuts out a word and pastes it at the bottom. Between two words a space is missing. Now the poster is finished.
questions: What does Mia do with the title?
Where does the photo come from?
Which keys does Mia press?
What is missing between two words?

translate.tr: Elif copies a photo from the internet.
wrong: Elif deletes a photo from the internet.
Elif copies a text from the internet.

informatik-a12-06-kalender:0.text:
David is sixteen and lives in Vienna. He has a calendar on his phone. His mother says: “You have an appointment at the dentist. The date is the tenth of March, at four o'clock.” David puts the appointment in right away. The app also shows the day of the week: Tuesday.

On Monday evening David gets a reminder. But on Tuesday at four he has football! That's exactly the same time. David calls the dentist and moves the appointment to Friday. Then he changes the date in the calendar. Now everything fits.

gloss.hast: (you) have; (einen Termin haben) have an appointment
gloss.an: at, on; (ruft … an) prefix of anrufen

questions: Where does David have his calendar?
On which day of the week is the appointment at first?
Why does David move the appointment?

translate.tr: David puts the appointment in the calendar.
wrong: David deletes the appointment from the calendar.
David moves the appointment in the calendar.

translate.tr: He moves the appointment to Friday.
wrong: He cancels the appointment on Friday.
He moves the appointment to Tuesday.

translate.tr: In the evening he gets a reminder.
wrong: In the morning he gets a reminder.
In the evening he sends a reminder.

informatik-a12-06-kalender:1.text:
It's Sophie's birthday on Saturday. She writes an invitation in the class group: “Party at my place, Saturday at seven!” Many friends answer right away. Only Paul says no. He has to work on Saturday and doesn't have the day off.

On Friday Sophie still has school. According to her timetable she has six lessons, including maths. On Saturday she doesn't set an alarm and sleeps late.

In the evening the guests come. Everyone is on time. They eat cake and talk about the summer holidays. At the end Paul comes after all. He has a present for Sophie.
questions: When is Sophie's birthday?
Why does Paul say no at first?
What do the guests do?
What are the guests like?

translate.tr: All the guests are on time.
wrong: Not all the guests are on time.

informatik-a12-07-probleme:0.text:
Felix is doing his computer science homework on the computer. Suddenly the computer freezes. The mouse doesn't work, and neither does the keyboard. Felix calls his father: “Help! My computer is broken!”

His father says: “Restart the computer. That's often the solution.” Felix restarts the computer, but the problem stays.

On Monday Felix goes to Mr Huber. He is the technician at school. Mr Huber finds the problem quickly: a program is too old. He fixes the computer in ten minutes. Felix is happy. Luckily he saved the file!

gloss.an: at, on; (ruf … an) prefix of anrufen

questions: What is Felix doing on the computer?
What does his father say?
Who fixes the computer?

informatik-a12-07-probleme:1.text:
Laura has a new tablet. She wants to watch a video, but there's no sound. She tries a lot of things: she turns the sound up and restarts the tablet. Nothing helps.

Her friend Nora has a tip: “Call the hotline! The tablet is still under warranty.” Laura calls. She has to wait twenty minutes. Then a man says: “Send the tablet to us. The repair is free.”

After a week the tablet comes back. Laura tries it out right away. The sound is back!

gloss.an: at, on; (ruft … an) prefix of anrufen
gloss.nach: after; (nach einer Woche) after a week

questions: What doesn't work on the tablet?
Who has a tip for Laura?
How long does Laura have to wait?
How much does the repair cost?

translate.tr: The tablet is still under warranty.
wrong: The tablet is no longer under warranty.
The phone is still under warranty.

informatik-a12-08-online-lernen:0.text:
Hanna is fifteen and lives in Vienna. She is taking an online course: programming for beginners. There is a new lesson every week.

Today Hanna watches the video for the third lesson. The video is twenty minutes long. Hanna puts on her headphones, because her brother is playing the guitar loudly.

After that the course has a live lesson. Hanna switches on the webcam. The teacher asks: “Hello! Who has a question?” Hanna wants to ask something, but her microphone doesn't work. She restarts the computer, and now it works.

At the end Hanna does the task. It isn't easy, but Hanna manages it.
questions: What is Hanna learning in the course?
Why does Hanna put on her headphones?
What doesn't work in the live lesson?

translate.tr: There is a new lesson every week.
wrong: There is a new lesson every day.
There is a new video every week.

informatik-a12-08-online-lernen:1.text:
Niko studies at TU Wien. In the evening he learns German online. The learning platform is simple: there he finds videos, texts and a chat.

Today the lesson is live. The teacher is speaking, but the sound is bad. Niko writes in the chat: “I can't hear anything!” A student has loud music on in his room. The teacher says: “Please, everyone, mute your microphone.” Now the sound is good.

After an hour everyone takes a break. Then the teacher revises the words from yesterday. On Friday Niko took a test. He passed it and is now getting a certificate.
questions: What is the problem in the live lesson?
What does the teacher do after the break?
What does Niko get after the test?

translate.tr: After an hour we take a break.
wrong: After an hour we take a test.
After a minute we take a break.

informatik-a12-09-spiele:0.text:
On Saturday Moritz is at his friend Laura's. Laura has a new games console. They play a car game together.

Each player drives a car. For every star there is a point. The first level is easy. At the end Moritz has twenty points and Laura only twelve. Moritz wins!

The second level is hard. Moritz drives too fast and loses. Laura laughs and wins. “The game is great,” says Moritz. In the evening they play for another hour.
questions: What does Laura have?
How many points does Laura have in the first level?
Who wins in the second level?

informatik-a12-09-spiele:1.text:
On Sunday Laura plays an old game on her own. Her character jumps over stones and water. The controller is new and works perfectly.

In every level there are enemies. They are fast and dangerous. Laura has three lives. In the fifth level she loses two lives. Now she only has one life left!

The finish is very close. Laura jumps, jumps again and makes it! She has a new record: eleven thousand points. Her mother calls: “Dinner!” But Laura says: “Just one more round, please!”
questions: How many lives does Laura have at the beginning?
Where does Laura lose two lives?
What does Laura say to her mother?

translate.tr: The character jumps over the water.
wrong: The character falls into the water.
The character jumped over the water.

translate.tr: I only have one life left.
wrong: He only has one life left.

informatik-a12-10-fotos-musik:0.text:
Emma and her class go on a trip to the Prater. Emma takes a lot of pictures: trees, animals and the Ferris wheel. At the end they all take a selfie together.

In the evening Emma is at home. In her gallery she now has a hundred pictures! Some pictures are too dark. Emma uses a filter, and the pictures are nice again.

Then she makes an album. It's called “Prater”. Emma shares the album with the class. The teacher writes: “Thank you, Emma! The pictures are great.”
questions: Where does the class go on a trip?
What is the problem with some pictures?
Who does Emma share the album with?

translate.tr: Emma takes a picture of the Ferris wheel.
wrong: Emma took a picture of the Ferris wheel.
All the pictures are too dark.

translate.tr: Emma shares the album with the class.
wrong: The class shares the album with Emma.

informatik-a12-10-fotos-musik:1.text:
Valentin studies at TU Wien and lives with Pia in a shared flat. Valentin likes listening to music. He streams songs on his phone every day.

On Friday it's Pia's birthday. Valentin makes a playlist for the party. It has fifty songs. The first song is by Falco, because Pia loves music from Austria.

In the evening a lot of friends come. The speaker is new and very loud. At eleven the neighbour knocks: “Quiet, please! I have to work early tomorrow.” Valentin turns the music down. The party goes on.
questions: What does Valentin stream the songs on?
How many songs does the playlist have?
What does the neighbour want?

wrong: Valentin doesn't like listening to music.

translate.tr: He makes a playlist for the party.
wrong: She makes a playlist for the party.
He listens to a playlist at the party.

mathe-a12-rechnen:0.text:
Paul is in his maths lesson. The teacher says: “Today we're doing mental arithmetic.” The first problem is easy: seven plus eight. Paul says: “Fifteen.” The result is correct.

Then comes the second problem: twenty minus six. Mia says: “Fourteen.” Correct too! Now it gets hard: nine times six. Paul thinks for a long time. “Fifty-four,” he says. Correct!

The last problem is a hundred divided by four. Nobody knows the result. The teacher laughs: “Twenty-five. This number is important!”
questions: How much is seven plus eight?
Which problem is hard?
Who knows the last result?

translate.tr: Today we're calculating in our heads.
wrong: Tomorrow we're calculating in our heads.

mathe-a12-rechnen:1.text:
Mia is doing her homework. Her father helps. The first problem: which numbers are even? Mia writes: two, four, seven. Her father says: “Seven is wrong. Seven is odd.”

The second problem: the sum of eleven and nine. Mia calculates and says: “Twenty.” And half of twenty? “Ten!”

The last problem is hard. Mia and her father solve it together. At the end they are both happy. Two plus two equals four — Mia has known that for a long time.

gloss.sie: she; they; (here) it — about the problem: die Aufgabe

questions: Which number is wrong?
What is half of twenty?
Who helps Mia?

wrong: The sum of twenty and ten.
We solve the problem on our own.

mathe-a12-02-grosse-zahlen:0.text:
Lena is doing her homework. The question is: how many inhabitants does Vienna have? Lena searches on the internet. Vienna has almost 2,000,000 inhabitants. That's two million. The number has seven digits.

Her brother Tom asks: “And Austria?” Austria has about nine million inhabitants. Tom counts the places: ones, tens, hundreds … That's hard!

Then Lena asks: “And how many people live on Earth?” The answer is: eight billion. Tom laughs: “So many zeros! I can't count that far.”
questions: How many inhabitants does Vienna have?
How many digits does the number have?
What can't Tom do?

mathe-a12-02-grosse-zahlen:1.text:
Mia is shopping at the supermarket. The milk costs 1.19 euros. That's a decimal number. Before the comma are the euros, after the comma are the cents.

Mia doesn't have much money. She estimates and rounds the prices. She rounds 1.19 euros down to 1 euro. The bread costs 2.85 euros. She rounds that up to 3 euros. Together that's about 4 euros.

At the checkout the woman says: “Exactly 4.04 euros, please.” Mia laughs. Her calculation was almost right. At home she shows her brother the prices on the number line.
questions: How much does the milk cost?
How does Mia round 2.85 euros?
How much does everything cost exactly?

translate.tr: The milk costs about one euro.
wrong: The milk costs exactly one euro.
The bread costs about one euro.

translate.tr: After the comma come the cents.
wrong: Before the comma come the cents.
After the comma come the euros.

mathe-a12-03-uhrzeit:0.text:
Today is sports day at school. At a quarter past eight the race starts. Mr Huber has a stopwatch. The children run a hundred metres.

Jonas runs fast. The stopwatch shows fifteen seconds. Sara needs only fourteen seconds. She wins!

After that Jonas looks at the clock on the wall. The big hand is on the six, the small hand between eight and nine. It's half past eight. Jonas asks: “How long is the break?” Mr Huber says: “Half an hour. At nine o'clock we carry on.” That's long enough for a sandwich and a glass of water.

gloss.halbe: half (eine halbe Stunde — half an hour)
gloss.geht: goes (es geht weiter — we carry on)

questions: When does the race start?
Who wins?
How long is the break?

translate.tr: The break lasts half an hour.
wrong: The lesson lasts half an hour.

mathe-a12-03-uhrzeit:1.text:
The Berger family is taking the train from Vienna to Salzburg. According to the timetable the departure is at 10:08. The train is on time. The journey takes two and a half hours.

In Linz they have to change. But today the second train is late: twenty minutes! Dad calculates: the arrival is now not at 12:38 but at 12:58.

At night Anna can't sleep. It's midnight. She writes to her friend in New York. There it's only six o'clock in the evening. The time difference is six hours.
questions: When is the departure?
Where do they have to change?
How big is the time difference?

translate.tr: The train is twenty minutes late.
wrong: The train is twenty minutes early.
The bus is twenty minutes late.

translate.tr: We have to change in Linz.
wrong: We have to get off in Linz.
We have to change in Vienna.

translate.tr: According to the timetable the train is on time.
wrong: According to the timetable the train is late.
The train is always on time.

mathe-a12-04-geld:0.text:
Paul gets ten euros pocket money every week. He wants to buy a bike. But the bike is expensive: it costs 240 euros.

Paul has a piggy bank. Every Saturday he puts a banknote in it. Sometimes he spends money on sweets. Then his mother says: “Spend less, then you can save more!”

After half a year Paul opens the piggy bank. He counts the coins and the notes. The amount is 210 euros. He still needs 30 euros. Paul calculates: that's three more weeks!

gloss.halben: half (ein halbes Jahr — half a year)

questions: How much pocket money does Paul get?
What does Paul want to buy?
How much money is still missing?

translate.tr: Paul is saving for a bike.
wrong: Paul is spending money on a bike.

mathe-a12-04-geld:1.text:
Finally Paul has enough money. He goes to the sports shop with his father. Today there's twenty euros off! The bike now costs only 220 euros. Paul also buys a bell for five euros. In total that's 225 euros.

Paul pays at the checkout with five fifty-euro notes. That's 250 euros. The shop assistant gives him 25 euros change and the receipt too.

Paul is happy: that was cheap! With the change he buys an ice cream for himself and for his father.
questions: How much discount is there today?
How much does everything cost in total?
What does Paul buy with the change?

translate.tr: The shop assistant gives back the change.
wrong: The shop assistant takes the change.
The shop assistant gives back the receipt.

mathe-a12-05-messen:0.text:
Emma is getting a new desk. But is there enough room in her bedroom? Dad gets the tape measure. Emma measures the wall: it's 2.40 metres long. The desk is 1.20 metres wide and 75 centimetres high. It fits!

In the afternoon Emma does her homework at the new desk. She has to draw a line with the ruler. The line is exactly twelve centimetres long.

Then Emma asks: “Dad, how far is my school?” Dad checks on his phone: “Two kilometres. You can go by bike.”
questions: How long is the wall?
What does Emma draw the line with?
How far is the school?

translate.tr: The school is two kilometres away.
wrong: The school is two metres away.
The school is twelve kilometres away.

mathe-a12-05-messen:1.text:
On Sunday Emma bakes a cake with Grandma. The recipe says: 250 grams of flour, 200 grams of sugar, half a litre of milk and a pound of butter.

Emma asks: “What's a pound?” Grandma laughs: “It's an old unit. A pound is 500 grams.” Emma puts the bowl on the scales. She weighs the flour. The flour is light, but the butter is heavy.

After an hour the cake is ready. It weighs almost a kilogram. Emma and Grandma eat two big pieces. Then the cake is a bit lighter.

gloss.halber: half (ein halber Liter — half a litre)
gloss.halben: half (einen halben Liter — half a litre)

questions: How many grams are in a pound?
What is heavy?
How much does the cake weigh?

translate.tr: We need half a litre of milk.
wrong: We need a litre of milk.
We need half a litre of water.

translate.tr: A pound is an old unit.
wrong: A pound is a new unit.
A kilogram is an old unit.

mathe-a12-06-formen:0.text:
In the art lesson Ms Novak says: “Today we're drawing a house. But you may only use shapes.”

Lukas takes a square for the house. For the roof he draws a triangle. The windows are small squares. The door is a rectangle. A rectangle has four corners, just like a square.

Next to the house Lukas draws a sun. The sun is round. Around the sun he draws lots of lines. At the end he puts a small dot on the door. That's the door handle! Ms Novak says: “Very nice, everything has corners, except the sun.”
questions: What shape is the roof?
What is round?
What is the dot on the door?

mathe-a12-06-formen:1.text:
It's Mum's birthday tomorrow. Lukas and his sister Mia have a present: a small glass ball. In the middle of the ball there is a star.

They need a box. The first box is flat. The ball doesn't fit in it. The second box is a cube. Mia says: “A cube has six faces, eight corners and twelve edges. The ball has no corners and no edges!”

The ball fits in the cube. Lukas sticks a golden star on the top of the box. Now the present is ready.
questions: What is in the middle of the ball?
How many edges does a cube have?
Why doesn't the ball fit in the first box?

mathe-a12-07-mathestunde:0.text:
Mr Wagner writes a problem on the board: 48 plus 37. “Today without a calculator! This is mental arithmetic.”

Sara puts her hand up right away. “85!” — “Correct. Please explain your working to us.” Sara says: “First I calculate 40 plus 30, that's 70. Then 8 plus 7, that's 15. And 70 plus 15 is 85.”

Max doesn't understand that. Mr Wagner explains it again slowly. Now Max understands the working too. At the end Mr Wagner says: “For homework you'll do ten problems. Without a calculator, please!”
questions: What is the problem on the board?
Who puts her hand up right away?
What is the homework?

translate.tr: Sara puts her hand up right away.
Please explain your working to us.
wrong: Please write the answer for us.
Please explain the problem to us.
Max still doesn't understand the problem.

mathe-a12-07-mathestunde:1.text:
Next week is the maths test. Max is nervous. He practises for half an hour every day. His sister helps him.

In the test Max sits next to Sara. Sara is very good at maths. But Max doesn't copy. He works everything out on his own.

A week later Mr Wagner marks the tests. Max has only two mistakes. He gets a 2, which means “good”. Max is happy. Mr Wagner says: “If you keep practising like this, maybe you'll have a 1 in your report.”

gloss.halbe: half (eine halbe Stunde — half an hour)
gloss.später: later (eine Woche später — a week later)

questions: How long does Max practise every day?
How many mistakes does Max have?
What grade does Max get?

translate.tr: Max is nervous before the test.
wrong: Max is happy before the test.
Max is nervous after the test.
Mr Wagner hands out the tests.

mathe-a12-08-anteile:0.text:
It's Tom's birthday. Eight children are at the party. Mum orders three pizzas. She divides each pizza into eight pieces. So one piece is an eighth.

Altogether there are 24 pieces. Mum calculates: 24 divided by 8 is 3. She shares out the pieces equally: each child gets three pieces.

But Lisa only eats two pieces. At the end one piece is left over. Tom is happy to take the rest. After that there's chocolate too. Mum divides it into three parts. One third is for Tom, one third for Lisa and one third for Dad.
questions: How many pieces does Mum divide each pizza into?
How many pieces does each child get?
Who takes the rest?

translate.tr: Mum divides the pizza into eight pieces.
wrong: Mum divides the pizza into three pieces.

translate.tr: At the end one piece is left over.
wrong: At the end no pieces are left over.
At the beginning one piece is left over.

mathe-a12-08-anteile:1.text:
Class 2B is planning a trip. There are 24 children in the class. Ms Novak says: “We'll vote. Each child has one vote.”

There are three ideas: the zoo, the museum and the swimming pool. The zoo gets 13 votes, the museum 6 and the swimming pool 5. The zoo has more than twice as many votes as the museum.

Ms Novak calculates: 13 out of 24, that's about 54 per cent. That's more than half, so it's the majority. But the zoo wins only narrowly. The share for the swimming pool is small. Even so, the whole class goes to the zoo.

gloss.so: as (so viele wie — as many as)

questions: How many votes does the zoo get?
Which idea has the majority?
About what percentage does the zoo have?

translate.tr: The majority wants to go to the zoo.
wrong: The minority wants to go to the zoo.
The majority wants to go to the museum.
The zoo wins by a wide margin.

mathe-a12-09-diagramme:0.text:
Ms Novak asks the class: “What pets do you have?” Lea makes a tally on the board. Seven children have a dog, five a cat and three a fish. Nine children don't have a pet.

Then they enter the numbers in a table. The table has two columns: “Animal” and “Number”. Each row has one animal.

At the end everyone draws a chart. Each bar is one animal. The longest bar is “no pet”. On the chart you can easily see: dogs are more popular than cats.
questions: How many children have a dog?
How many columns does the table have?
What is the longest bar?

mathe-a12-09-diagramme:1.text:
For a week Jonas measures the temperature every day at noon. On Monday it's 12 degrees, on Tuesday 14 and on Wednesday 17 degrees. The temperature rises until Thursday. On Thursday is the highest value: 20 degrees. Then it falls again: Friday 18, Saturday 13, Sunday 11 degrees.

Jonas draws a curve. It goes up first and then down. Then he calculates the average: the sum is 105, and 105 divided by 7 is 15. So on average it was 15 degrees.

At the end Jonas compares the week with last week. This week was warmer.

gloss.lang: for (eine Woche lang — for a week)

questions: When is the temperature highest?
What is the average?
What was this week like?

translate.tr: On average it was fifteen degrees.
wrong: On average it was fifty degrees.

mathe-a12-10-raetsel:0.text:
Lena visits her grandpa. Grandpa always has a puzzle for her. Today he writes a sequence on a sheet of paper: 2, 4, 8, 16 … “How does the sequence continue?”

Lena guesses: “Twenty?” Grandpa shakes his head: “Wrong, I'm afraid.” Then he gives her a hint: “Look at the pattern. Each number is twice as big as the number before it.”

Now Lena understands the rule: always times two! She continues the sequence: 32, 64, 128. Grandpa laughs: “Correct! Puzzling is fun, isn't it?” Lena wants a new puzzle right away.

gloss.geht: goes (wie geht … weiter — how does … continue)
gloss.oder: or; (at the end of a question) isn't it?

questions: What does Lena guess first?
What rule does the sequence have?
Who gives the hint?

translate.tr: Each number is twice as big.
wrong: Each number is half as big.

mathe-a12-10-raetsel:1.text:
In the evening Lena plays chess with Grandpa. Grandpa always has a good strategy and almost always wins. Lena doesn't like losing.

Today Lena thinks for a long time. But then she makes a bad move and loses her queen. Grandpa says: “Never mind. Keep playing!” In the end nobody has won. The game ends in a draw. Lena is pleased.

After that Lena also solves a sudoku from the newspaper. It has 81 squares. Each square gets a digit from 1 to 9. Each digit may appear only once in a row.
questions: Who almost always wins?
How does the game end today?
How many squares does the sudoku have?

translate.tr: The game ends in a draw.
wrong: The game ends in a win.

cyber-a2-angriffe:0.text:
Jonas studies computer science at TU Wien and works part-time in the IT department. On Monday there was an attack on the library's server. An attacker found a vulnerability in old software and exploited it.

His boss, Ms Berger, explains to him: “The attacker could only exploit the security hole because nobody installed the update.” Luckily the data was safe, because the encryption worked. The attacker only saw unreadable characters.

Now the team has to check all systems. Ms Berger also says that all students should turn on two-factor authentication. In the evening Jonas writes a message to his friends: “Please encrypt your hard drives and turn on two-factor authentication! It only takes five minutes.”
questions: What did the attacker exploit?
Why could the attacker exploit the security hole?
Why was the data safe?
What should all students do?

wrong: The attacker is looking for a vulnerability.
The attacker didn't find a vulnerability.
The encryption didn't protect the data.

cyber-a2-angriffe:1.text:
On Friday Lena, a student at TU Wien, gets an email. The sender is supposedly the rector's office: “Your access to TISS ends today. Click on the link and enter your password!” Lena becomes suspicious, because the address looks strange. She thinks: this must be a phishing email!

She doesn't click on the link but reports the email to the IT department. Jonas works there. He explains to her that attackers steal passwords with emails like this. Sometimes there is also malware in the attachment. If you open the attachment, an attacker can access the computer.

“The firewall blocks a lot, but not everything,” says Jonas. “That's why a backup is so important.” In the evening Lena makes a backup of her hard drive. Now she feels much safer.
questions: Who supposedly sent the email?
Why does Lena become suspicious?
What does Lena do with the email?
What does Lena do in the evening?

translate.tr: Lena reports the phishing email to the IT department.
wrong: Lena forwards the phishing email to her friends.
Jonas reports the phishing email to the IT department.
Lena doesn't report the phishing email to the IT department.

translate.tr: The attackers want to steal passwords.
wrong: The attackers have already stolen passwords.
The attackers want to change passwords.
The attackers want to steal data.

cyber-a21-02-passwoerter:0.text:
Katharina is in her first semester at TU Wien. She lives with Florian in a shared flat. Florian uses the same password for all his accounts because he can remember it easily. Katharina says: “You should never reuse passwords. If an attacker knows one password, he tries it on your other accounts too.”

Then she shows him her password manager. The program creates long passwords with capital letters, digits and special characters. “Length matters most,” Katharina explains. “A computer can guess a short password quickly.”

Florian isn't sure: “And where are my passwords then?” Katharina laughs: “In the password manager, of course. You only have to remember one password.”
questions: Why does Florian always use the same password?
According to Katharina, what matters most?
What does an attacker do with a password he knows?
How many passwords does Florian have to remember with the password manager?

translate.tr: A computer can guess a short password quickly.
wrong: A computer can guess a long password quickly.
A computer can't guess a short password quickly.
A computer can save a short password quickly.

translate.tr: I only have to remember one password.
wrong: I have to remember all the passwords.
I only have to write down one password.

cyber-a21-02-passwoerter:1.text:
Two weeks later Florian reads in the news about a data breach: an online shop has lost millions of passwords. Luckily he has already changed his old password.

In the tutorial the tutor, Verena, shows how attackers crack passwords. In a dictionary attack a program tries out lots of well-known words. The password “sonnenschein” is cracked after a few seconds. A random password with twenty characters is much more secure.

For his master password Florian now uses a passphrase of four random words, for example “Kaffee Fenster Wolke Gitarre”. He can remember it easily. The password manager stores all the other passwords for him.

gloss.zum: zum Beispiel — for example; zum Glück — luckily

questions: Where did Florian read about the data breach?
What does a program do in a dictionary attack?
What does Florian's passphrase consist of?

translate.tr: Attackers can crack short passwords quickly.
wrong: Attackers can't crack short passwords quickly.
Attackers can steal short passwords quickly.

translate.tr: The password manager stores all passwords.
wrong: The password manager deletes all passwords.
The password manager stored all passwords.

translate.tr: A random password is hard to guess.
wrong: A random password is easy to guess.
A short password is hard to guess.

cyber-a21-03-phishing:0.text:
Nina studies at TU Wien and works twice a week in the IT support of a small company. On Tuesday Ms Berger from accounting calls: “There's an email from the bank in my inbox. The subject line says: Urgent! Your account will be blocked.”

Nina comes to her right away. The email has an attachment called “Rechnung.zip”. Nina says: “Please don't click on anything!” Then she shows Ms Berger the sender address: it doesn't end with the bank's name but with a strange domain. Besides, the text has a lot of spelling mistakes.

“The email is fake,” Nina explains. “A real bank never writes like that.” Ms Berger is glad that she called first.
questions: Who got the email?
What does the subject line say?
How does Nina know the email is fake?

translate.tr: There's an urgent email in my inbox.
wrong: There's a fake email in my inbox.
There's no urgent email in my inbox.

translate.tr: The text has a lot of spelling mistakes.
wrong: The text has no spelling mistakes.
The text has a lot of links.

cyber-a21-03-phishing:1.text:
After this email Nina explains to all her colleagues how to recognise phishing. “Be suspicious when an email asks you to do something: to pay quickly or enter your login details. That's almost always a fake.”

Mr Novak asks: “And what do I do with an email like that? Should I just delete it?” Nina answers: “No, first forward it to IT support. Then we can see whether other colleagues got the email too. After that you can delete it.”

Later she also shows her colleagues the spam folder. There Mr Novak finds three more phishing emails. He laughs: “I never saw those!”
questions: When should you be suspicious?
What should you do first with a phishing email?
How many phishing emails does Mr Novak find in the spam folder?

translate.tr: I forward the email to IT support.
wrong: I forwarded the email to IT support.
I delete the email from IT support.

translate.tr: The email asks me to pay.
wrong: The email doesn't ask me to pay.
The email asks me to call.
This website is not a fake.

cyber-a21-04-social-engineering:0.text:
Miriam studies computer science and works part-time at an insurance company in Vienna. On Thursday she gets a call. A man says: “Hello, this is Stefan from IT support. We have a problem with your account. I need your password quickly, otherwise you'll lose all your data.”

The man is friendly, but he puts on a lot of pressure. Miriam is helpful and doesn't want any problems. Still, she thinks: a real IT support employee never asks for your password.

She says: “I'll call you right back.” Then she calls the real IT department. Nobody there knows a Stefan. The caller was a scammer. He posed as a colleague because he wanted to win her trust. But Miriam didn't let herself be fooled.

gloss.lassen: to let (sich täuschen lassen — to let yourself be fooled)

questions: Who does the caller pretend to be?
What does the man want from Miriam?
What does Miriam do after the call?

translate.tr: The caller puts on a lot of pressure.
wrong: The caller doesn't put on any pressure.
The caller is in a big hurry.

translate.tr: A scammer wants to win our trust.
wrong: A scammer wants to steal our data.
A scammer wanted to win our trust.

cyber-a21-04-social-engineering:1.text:
A week later the insurance company holds a training session on social engineering. The trainer says: “Last year a man came to the entrance with a high-visibility vest and a fake ID. He seemed believable, and someone held the door open for him.”

Then she shows a USB stick. “We put this stick in the car park as a test. Ten employees found it, and eight plugged it into their computer. Curiosity is often stronger than caution.”

Miriam talks about her call. The trainer praises her: “Exactly right! Never reveal your password, not even on the phone. If you take your time, you won't fall for it so quickly.”

gloss.nimmt: takes (sich Zeit nehmen — to take your time)

questions: How did the man in the high-visibility vest get into the company?
How many employees plugged in the USB stick?
Why does the trainer praise Miriam?

translate.tr: The man had a fake ID.
wrong: The man had a real ID.
The man doesn't have a fake ID.

translate.tr: Curiosity is often stronger than caution.
wrong: Curiosity is never stronger than caution.
Caution is often stronger than curiosity.

cyber-a21-05-patches:0.text:
Mia studies electrical engineering at TU Wien and helps in the lab twice a week. On Tuesday the technician, Mr Huber, shows her a list. On many computers the graphics card driver is outdated.

“Yesterday the vendor released a security update for the driver,” Mr Huber explains. “It closes a dangerous hole. We have to apply the patch today.” Mia asks why it's so urgent. He answers that attackers often attack outdated systems within a few days.

First they update Mr Huber's computer. Then Mia applies the patch on the other devices. That takes three hours. In the evening all the computers are up to date, and Mr Huber is pleased.
questions: What is outdated on many computers?
Who released the security update?
Why is the patch so urgent?
What are the computers like in the evening?

translate.tr: The driver on this computer is outdated.
wrong: The driver on this computer is new.
The program on this computer is outdated.
The driver on that computer is outdated.
The vendor will release a patch.
The vendor didn't release a patch.

translate.tr: Mia is installing the security update today.
wrong: Mia is deleting the security update today.
Mia is installing the security update tomorrow.

cyber-a21-05-patches:1.text:
Mr Huber is planning maintenance in the university's data centre for Saturday. Mia is supposed to help him. A new update for the mail server is very important because it fixes a critical bug. This bug fix matters for all students.

Unfortunately the room-planning program isn't compatible with the update. So a colleague wants to postpone the maintenance. But Mr Huber says: “We can't postpone it. Next month is the end of support for the old version anyway.”

On Saturday they install the update. After that the mail server doesn't start any more. Mia stays calm: she rolls back the update, and the server runs again. On Monday they find the cause and try again.
questions: When is Mr Huber planning the maintenance?
Why is the update so important?
What does a colleague want to do?
What does Mia do when the mail server doesn't start?

translate.tr: The program isn't compatible with the update.
wrong: The program is compatible with the update.
The server isn't compatible with the update.

cyber-a21-06-surfen:0.text:
Sara studies business informatics at TU Wien. Her grandpa Karl wants to buy a train ticket online for the first time and calls her. At the weekend she visits him.

First Sara shows him the address bar. “Do you see the little padlock? That means the connection is encrypted,” she explains. “If the padlock is missing, you don't enter any data.”

Then a window about cookies opens. Karl wants to accept everything right away, but Sara says: “Better click on ‘Only necessary cookies’.” At the end she also installs an ad blocker for her grandpa. He doesn't want an extension for passwords: “That's too complicated for me!”

gloss.mal: time (zum ersten Mal — for the first time)

questions: What does Grandpa Karl want to buy online?
What does the little padlock mean?
Which cookies should Karl accept?
What does Sara install at the end?

translate.tr: Do you see the padlock in the address bar?
wrong: Do you see the link in the address bar?
Do you (formal) see the padlock in the address bar?

cyber-a21-06-surfen:1.text:
David lives in a student hall in Vienna. In the evening he's looking for cheap headphones online. Suddenly a pop-up opens: “Congratulations! You've won a phone!” David is about to press the button, but then he sees a warning from the browser.

The site isn't trustworthy, because a redirect has sent him to an unknown address. David closes the window right away.

The next day he tells his flatmate Sara about it. She says: “Well done! Now clear your history and your cache.” David asks whether incognito mode protects him. “No,” Sara laughs. “Incognito mode just doesn't save any history. It doesn't help against fraud.”
questions: What is David looking for online?
Why doesn't David press the button?
Why isn't the site trustworthy?
What does Sara say about incognito mode?

wrong: The browser doesn't show a warning.

cyber-a21-07-privatsphaere:0.text:
Nora is in the final year of a grammar school in Vienna and wants to study at TU next year. For maths she downloads a new learning app. A long window appears right away: the app wants her consent for tracking.

Her brother Felix studies computer science and looks over her shoulder. “Read the privacy policy first,” he says. It says that the app collects a lot of data, for example her contacts.

Nora thinks that's strange. “Why does a maths app need my contacts?” Felix explains: “Data protection in the EU is strict. Without your consent the app can't store everything.” So Nora says no to tracking. She only agrees to notifications. “If you change your mind, you can withdraw your consent at any time,” says Felix. Her privacy matters to Nora.

gloss.änderst: (you) change (Meinung ändern — to change your mind)

questions: What does Nora want to do next year?
What does the privacy policy say?
What does Nora say no to?
Who explains data protection to Nora?

translate.tr: The app collects a lot of data.
wrong: The app deletes a lot of data.

cyber-a21-07-privatsphaere:1.text:
In his seminar at TU, Felix gives a short presentation about advertising on the internet. He explains to his fellow students: “Many apps are free because the provider makes money with our data.”

A provider analyses user behaviour: which sites do we visit? How long do we watch a video? Some companies also sell this data to other companies. That's how personalised advertising comes about.

A student asks whether you can be anonymous online. Felix answers: “You're almost never completely anonymous. But you can do a lot. Turn off the advertising ID on your phone and use a different browser.” At the end he says: “Not every data collection is surveillance, but we should be careful.”

gloss.hält: holds (ein Referat halten — to give a presentation)

questions: What is Felix's presentation about?
Why are many apps free?
What do some companies do with the data?
What should you turn off on your phone?

translate.tr: Turn off the adverts on your phone!
wrong: Turn on the adverts on your phone!
Turn off the adverts on your laptop!

cyber-a21-08-mobil:0.text:
Emir studies electrical engineering at TU Wien. At the weekend he's looking for a torch app in the app store. He finds a free app and downloads it onto his device.

When it first starts, the app wants a lot of permissions: location, contacts and the microphone. Emir is surprised, because a torch only needs the light. He asks Katharina. She works as a tutor in the university's security lab.

Katharina says: “Deny the app access! Good apps only ask for the permissions they really need. Read the reviews too, because not every developer is trustworthy.”

Emir deletes the app. Now he checks the app permissions for every new app. He only allows what the app really needs.
questions: What is Emir looking for in the app store?
Why is Emir surprised?
What does Katharina advise?
What does Emir do at the end?

translate.tr: The app wants my location and my contacts.
wrong: The app wants my microphone and my contacts.
The app doesn't want my location and my contacts.

cyber-a21-08-mobil:1.text:
On Friday evening Katharina takes the underground home. At home she notices: her phone is gone! Did she lose it, or was it stolen?

Luckily she turned on location tracking a month ago. She logs in on her laptop and can locate the phone. It's at an underground station at Karlsplatz. She calls the lost and found, but nobody there has her phone.

Her brother says: “If you don't find it again, wipe all the data remotely and block the SIM card!”

But the next morning the lost and found calls: a woman found the phone on the underground and handed it in. In the afternoon Katharina picks it up. Her data is safe because the phone was locked.

gloss.hause: home (nach Hause — home; zu Hause — at home)
gloss.vor: ago (vor einem Monat — a month ago)

questions: Where did Katharina lose her phone?
Why can Katharina locate the phone?
What does her brother advise?
Who calls the next morning?

translate.tr: I lost my phone on the underground.
wrong: I found my phone on the underground.
I lost my phone on the bus.
I'll lose my phone on the underground.

translate.tr: With location tracking you can find the phone.
wrong: With location tracking you can't find the phone.
With the lost and found you can find the phone.

cyber-a21-09-backups:0.text:
Felix studies architecture at TU Wien. For weeks he has been writing an important term paper. The file is only on his laptop and on an old USB stick.

On Tuesday the laptop won't start any more. The hard drive is broken. Felix plugs in the USB stick, but he only finds an old copy there. Last week he deleted the new file by accident because he needed space. That's a big data loss!

His flatmate Sara studies computer science. She says: “You have to back up your data regularly, ideally on an external hard drive and in a second place too.” Felix buys a hard drive right away. But he's sad because he has to write many pages again.

gloss.schreibt: writes (schreiben an — to work on a text)
gloss.ein: prefix (steckt ein — plugs in); a, one

questions: What does Felix study?
Why won't the laptop start?
What does Felix find on the USB stick?
What does Sara advise?

translate.tr: My laptop's hard drive is broken.
wrong: My laptop's hard drive is working.
My laptop's USB stick is broken.

translate.tr: I deleted the file by accident.
wrong: I deleted the file on purpose.
I saved the file by accident.
He deleted the file by accident.

translate.tr: You have to back up your data regularly.
wrong: You have to delete your data regularly.
You don't have to back up your data regularly.
We have to back up our data regularly.

cyber-a21-09-backups:1.text:
Alongside her studies Sara works in the IT support of an institute. On Monday malware encrypted all the folders on the server. The staff are nervous because they can't work.

But Sara's boss stays calm. The institute makes a backup every night on a fixed schedule. They keep the copies in two storage locations: on hard drives in another building and in cloud storage.

First they replace the hard drives in the server with new ones. Then they restore the data from Sunday. The backup is complete; only one day's work is missing. Sara learns: a backup is only good if you can actually restore it.
questions: What happened on Monday?
When does the institute make a backup?
Where does the institute keep the copies?
What is missing after the restore?

translate.tr: The backup runs every night on schedule.
wrong: The backup runs every week on schedule.
The backup doesn't run every night on schedule.

translate.tr: We restore the data from Sunday.
wrong: We delete the data from Sunday.
We restored the data from Sunday.
We restore the data from Monday.

translate.tr: The copies are in a different storage location.
wrong: The copies are in the same storage location.
The files are in a different storage location.

cyber-a21-10-konten:0.text:
Laura studies business informatics at TU Wien. On Thursday at midnight she gets a notification: “Unusual login to your account from Brazil. Was that you?” Laura has never been to Brazil.

She opens the app and sees the latest activity. There were ten login attempts in one hour. Someone tried the password and also the security question. The answer was easy: the name of her cat.

Laura clicks on “That wasn't me” and confirms it with a code. The service blocks the account temporarily because it wants to prevent unauthorised access. The next day Laura changes her password and chooses a new security question with a difficult answer.
questions: Where did the unusual login come from?
How many login attempts were there in one hour?
What was the answer to the security question?
Why does the service block the account?

translate.tr: The answer to the security question was too easy.
wrong: The answer to the security question was too difficult.

cyber-a21-10-konten:1.text:
Laura's friend David was less lucky. A hacker took over his account on a gaming platform and changed the password. Now David is locked out of his own account. He didn't notice the attack in time because the notifications went to an old email address.

Laura helps him, and together they start the recovery. First David writes to support. Support wants to know whether the account really belongs to him. David has to prove it. In a video call he shows his ID. As further proof he also names his last purchases in the game.

After three days he gets his account back. Now he has a new email address in the account and two-factor authentication.

gloss.tagen: days (nach drei Tagen — after three days)

questions: Why didn't David notice the attack in time?
Who does David write to first?
How does David prove that the account belongs to him?
When does David get his account back?

translate.tr: A hacker has taken over my account.
wrong: A hacker has deleted my account.
A hacker has taken over your account.
A hacker hasn't taken over my account.

translate.tr: I'm locked out of my account.
wrong: I have access to my account.
He's locked out of his account.

translate.tr: You have to prove that the account belongs to you.
wrong: You have to prove that the account belongs to him.
You don't have to prove that the account belongs to you.
I have to prove that the account belongs to me.

informatik-a2-software:0.text:
Sophie is in her first semester of computer science. Today she has her first practical class in the computer room at TU Wien. But the room is full, and the connection to the server is very slow. The tutor, Paul, says: “The network has a problem today. We'll have to wait a bit.”

Sophie wants to install a program, but it doesn't work. Her laptop still has an old operating system. Paul explains that she has to update the operating system first. The update takes almost half an hour.

After that Sophie starts the program, but it shows an error. Sophie is nervous because the class will soon be over. Paul looks at the error and laughs: “You just entered the wrong password!” Sophie laughs too. Luckily everything works now.

gloss.geht: works (das geht nicht — it doesn't work)
gloss.halbe: half (eine halbe Stunde — half an hour)

questions: Why is the connection to the server so slow?
Why can't Sophie install the program?
How long does the update take?
What was the error?

translate.tr: The connection to the server is very slow.
wrong: The connection to the server is very fast.
The connection to the server was very slow.

translate.tr: She has to update the operating system first.
wrong: She has to install the operating system first.
He has to update the operating system first.
Later she has to update the operating system.
The program doesn't show an error.

informatik-a2-software:1.text:
Mehmet and Sophie are programming a small application together for their project. The application is meant to help students by showing free study rooms at the university. Mehmet already knows Java, but for the project they're using Python. Sophie thinks Python is a good programming language for beginners.

On Wednesday they test the app with ten users. Suddenly an error message appears: “Not enough storage”. The hard drive of Mehmet's laptop is almost full, because he has saved a lot of films on it.

Sophie laughs and first deletes a few old files. Then they save the data on the university server. After that the application works without problems, and the users are happy. Mehmet says: “Next week I'll clean up my hard drive, I promise!”
questions: What does the application show?
Which programming language do they use for the project?
Why is the hard drive almost full?
Where do they save the data in the end?

translate.tr: Python is a good programming language for beginners.
wrong: Python is a good programming language for professionals.
Java is a good programming language for beginners.
Python is a bad programming language for beginners.

translate.tr: The hard drive is almost full.
wrong: The hard drive is almost empty.
The hard drive is completely full.

informatik-a21-02-netz-zu-hause:0.text:
Valentina studies electrical engineering at TU Wien and has lived in a shared flat since October. On the first evening there's no internet. Her flatmate Kerstin says: “The provider sent the modem ages ago, but nobody has connected it.”

Valentina finds the modem and the router in a box. She connects the two devices with a network cable. After ten minutes a green light comes on, and the Wi-Fi works.

Kerstin is happy because now she can work in bed without cables. But in Valentina's room the signal is weak. So she runs a long network cable through the hall to her computer. Kerstin laughs: “You really are a technician!”
questions: Who sent the modem?
What does Valentina connect the two devices with?
Why is Kerstin happy?
Where is the signal weak?

translate.tr: She connects the router to the modem.
wrong: He connects the router to the modem.
She disconnects the router from the modem.
She connects the computer to the modem.

translate.tr: In her room the signal is weak.
wrong: In her room the signal is strong.
In his room the signal is weak.
In the kitchen the signal is weak.

informatik-a21-02-netz-zu-hause:1.text:
In November the internet in the flat suddenly gets very slow. Valentina measures the speed: it's much lower than in the contract. At first she thinks of an outage, but there's nothing on the provider's website.

Then she notices that Kerstin watches series in high quality every evening. That needs a lot of bandwidth. Besides, the router's range is too small for the big flat.

Valentina buys an extender and sets it up in the hall. For that she needs the login details printed on the bottom of the router. Now the signal is good everywhere. But the two girls know: next year the building is getting fibre optics, and then there will finally be enough bandwidth for everyone.
questions: Why does the flat need so much bandwidth?
Where does Valentina set up the extender?
Where are the login details?
What is the building getting next year?

translate.tr: The router's range is too small.
wrong: The router's range is big enough.
The router's speed is too low.

translate.tr: Valentina sets up the extender in the hall.
wrong: Valentina sets up the router in the hall.
Valentina switches off the extender in the hall.
Valentina sets up the extender in the kitchen.

translate.tr: At first she thinks it's an outage.
wrong: Later she thinks it's an outage.
At first he thinks it's an outage.
At first she thinks it's a virus.

informatik-a21-03-benutzeroberflaeche:0.text:
Jakob studies computer science at TU Wien. On Sunday he visits his grandma Hilde. She has a new laptop, but the user interface is completely unfamiliar to her.

First Jakob shows her the taskbar at the bottom of the screen. There are small icons for the most important programs there. “If you double-click on an icon, a window opens,” he explains. Grandma Hilde tries it, but the mouse pointer keeps jumping too far.

Then Jakob opens the menu and shows her the button for switching off. Grandma is pleased: “Now I can read emails and switch the laptop off again. I don't need any more than that!”
questions: What is completely unfamiliar to Grandma Hilde?
Where is the taskbar?
What happens when you double-click on an icon?
What does Jakob show her in the menu?

translate.tr: The taskbar is at the bottom of the screen.
wrong: The taskbar is at the top of the screen.
The menu is at the bottom of the screen.

translate.tr: The mouse pointer keeps jumping too far.
wrong: The mouse pointer sometimes jumps too far.
The mouse pointer keeps moving too slowly.

informatik-a21-03-benutzeroberflaeche:1.text:
A week later Grandma Hilde calls: “The letters are so small, I can't read anything!” Jakob comes round again and opens the settings.

First he sets the font size to the maximum. Then he selects a different view so that the icons are bigger. In the evening the bright screen is tiring for Grandma's eyes, so Jakob turns on dark mode.

Finally he moves the most important programs to the taskbar. “You see, Grandma? You can adapt almost everything to your own wishes.” Grandma Hilde laughs: “Then please adapt my grandson too. He should visit me more often!”
questions: Why does Grandma Hilde call?
What does Jakob do so that the icons are bigger?
Why does Jakob turn on dark mode?
What does Grandma Hilde wish for at the end?

translate.tr: He sets the font size to the maximum.
wrong: He sets the font size to the minimum.
She sets the font size to the maximum.
He sets the brightness to the maximum.

translate.tr: In the evening he turns on dark mode.
wrong: In the morning he turns on dark mode.
In the evening he turns off dark mode.

informatik-a21-04-hardware:0.text:
Emre likes playing on the computer, but his old PC is too slow. His friend Lukas studies computer engineering and suggests: “Let's build a new computer together!”

On Saturday they order the parts. First they mount the processor and the RAM on the motherboard. Then they put the motherboard into the case. The graphics card is the most expensive part, because Emre wants to play modern games.

Finally they connect the power supply to all the parts. Emre presses the button, but nothing happens. Lukas looks for the problem and laughs: “The switch on the power supply is off!” At last the fans turn, and the hardware works.
questions: Why do Emre and Lukas want to build a new computer?
What do they mount on the motherboard first?
Why do they buy an expensive graphics card?
Why doesn't the computer work at first?

translate.tr: The graphics card is the most expensive part.
wrong: The graphics card is the cheapest part.
The processor is the most expensive part.

translate.tr: They put the motherboard into the case.
wrong: They take the motherboard out of the case.
He puts the motherboard into the case.
They put the graphics card into the case.

informatik-a21-04-hardware:1.text:
Emre's sister Derya starts her studies at TU Wien in the autumn. She needs a new device that she can take to university every day. Emre wants to recommend a gaming laptop, but Derya says: “I don't need huge performance. Battery life is much more important to me.”

In the shop they compare three laptops. The first is very powerful but heavy. The second has too few ports, and you can't connect a monitor. The third is light, lasts ten hours and has enough ports.

Derya takes the third one. The shop assistant explains that you can upgrade the RAM later. “Great,” says Derya, “then I can simply swap this component in two years.”

gloss.jahren: years (in zwei Jahren — in two years)

questions: What is most important to Derya?
What is the problem with the second laptop?
Which laptop does Derya take?
What can you upgrade later?

translate.tr: Battery life is much more important to me.
wrong: Battery life isn't important to me at all.
Performance is much more important to me.

translate.tr: The first laptop is very powerful.
wrong: The second laptop is very powerful.
The first laptop is very light.
The first laptop isn't very powerful.

informatik-a21-05-web:0.text:
Nora is seventeen and wants to study computer science at TU Wien after her Matura. In the evening she looks for information about the degree on the internet. She types the university's web address into the address bar and opens the home page.

The page is long, and Nora has to scroll a lot. She opens every interesting page in a new tab. After ten minutes she has twelve tabs open and can't find anything any more.

Her brother Max laughs: “Save the important pages as bookmarks, then you can close the tabs.”

The next day Nora no longer knows where she read the information about admission. Luckily there's the history. There she finds all the pages from yesterday. Then she searches again. The first two search results are just adverts, but the third one is right.
questions: What does Nora do with every interesting page?
What does Max advise his sister?
Where does Nora find the pages from yesterday?
What does Nora want to do after her Matura?

translate.tr: She opens the university's home page.
wrong: She closes the university's home page.
He opens the university's home page.
She opens the school's home page.

translate.tr: Save the page as a bookmark!
wrong: Delete the page from your bookmarks!
Save the page to your history!

translate.tr: The first two search results are just adverts.
wrong: The last two search results are just adverts.
The first two search results aren't adverts.

informatik-a21-05-web:1.text:
In summer TU Wien offers a programming course for school students. Nora wants to take part and has to fill in a form online. She writes her name, her school and her email address. She forgets one field, but it's a required field. The page shows a red message, and Nora fills in the field.

Then she has to upload her school report. Unfortunately the file size is too big. Max helps her make the file smaller, and now it works.

After the course Nora writes a post for her school's blog. She says that the course content was exciting. Her teacher reads the text and publishes it on Friday.
questions: What did Nora forget in the form at first?
Why can't Nora upload the report at first?
Who publishes Nora's post?

translate.tr: Nora has to fill in a form.
wrong: Nora has to send a form.
Nora doesn't have to fill in a form.

informatik-a21-06-apps:0.text:
In the summer Amir is doing an internship at a small company in Vienna. The team there builds apps, and Amir works with Clara. She is a developer, and Amir wants to become a developer later too. Their new project is an app for the university canteen: students should be able to see which food is on today.

First they talk about the target group. Clara says: “Our users have little time. The app has to be user-friendly.” That's why the app gets only three features.

Amir draws a sketch on paper. Then together they design the layout and a simple prototype on the computer. On Friday five students test the prototype. Their feedback is positive; only the font is too small.
questions: What should the app show?
Why does the app get only three features?
What did Amir draw on paper?
What was the problem with the prototype?

translate.tr: The app has to be user-friendly.
wrong: The app doesn't have to be user-friendly.

informatik-a21-06-apps:1.text:
In August the team develops the real app. It's supposed to run on two platforms: Android and iOS. Amir optimises the font and the colours because the users asked for that.

After three weeks the first version is ready. But on the first day there's a crash when you click on Monday's menu. Clara finds the bug quickly, and the next day a new version comes out.

Now every user gets a notification at eleven o'clock with the dish of the day. In the app store the app already has lots of good ratings. Clara says to Amir: “We have to keep improving the app, but you worked very well during your internship.”
questions: Which platforms should the app run on?
When did the app crash?
What do the users get at eleven o'clock?

translate.tr: Amir optimises the app for small phones.
wrong: Amir optimises the app for big phones.
Clara optimises the app for small phones.

translate.tr: The app has lots of good ratings.
wrong: The app has lots of bad ratings.
The app has few good ratings.

informatik-a21-07-datenbanken:0.text:
Felix goes to an HTL in Vienna and helps in the school library in the afternoons. Until now all the books have been in a long list. The list isn't clear, and many books are in it twice.

So Felix builds a small database. It has one table for the books and one table for the students. Each book is an entry with title, author and category, for example crime, novel or computer science.

For two days Felix enters all the books. After that the program shows all the titles in alphabetical order. The librarian, Ms Novak, is delighted: “Finally I can find a book in ten seconds!”

gloss.lang: for (zwei Tage lang — for two days)

questions: Where does Felix help in the afternoons?
What was the problem with the old list?
How many tables does the database have?
How does the program show the titles?

translate.tr: Each book is an entry in the table.
wrong: Each student is an entry in the table.
Each book is a category in the table.

informatik-a21-07-datenbanken:1.text:
Now Ms Novak can query the database. For example, she enters the search term “Krimi” and immediately sees all the crime novels in the library's collection. She can also ask which students brought a book back too late.

Felix explains to her how to manage the database. Only Ms Novak and Felix have access, because students' names are in it too. You can choose the order of the books yourself: by title or by date.

At the end Felix says: “The backup is important. Every Friday we copy the database to an external hard drive.” After a month the database is complete, and nobody needs the old list any more.

gloss.einmal: once (einmal im Monat — once a month)

questions: What does Ms Novak see when she enters “Krimi”?
Why do only two people have access?
When is the backup made?

wrong: The database used to be complete.

informatik-a21-08-team:0.text:
Elif studies computer science at TU Wien. This semester she's working on a project with three other students: they're developing an app for the university canteen. On Monday they have their first meeting in the library.

Niklas is the team leader. He says: “The deadline is the end of January. We need a schedule, otherwise we won't make it.” Then he assigns the tasks. Elif is responsible for the database, because she's already done that during her internship. Mara does the design, and Niklas writes the code for the server.

Every Friday each team member writes a short message about their work. At the end of the meeting everyone is happy, because the tasks are clear now.
questions: What is the team working on?
When is the deadline?
Why is Elif responsible for the database?
What does each team member write on Friday?

translate.tr: We need a schedule for the project.
wrong: We don't need a schedule for the project.
We need a budget for the project.
We have a schedule for the project.

translate.tr: Niklas assigns the tasks in the team.
wrong: Niklas does the tasks in the team.
Niklas assigned the tasks in the team.
Niklas gets the tasks in the team.

translate.tr: Elif is responsible for the database.
wrong: Elif is responsible for the design.
Elif isn't responsible for the database.
Mara is responsible for the database.

informatik-a21-08-team:1.text:
Three weeks later the team has a video conference because Mara is ill. Niklas asks about progress, because the first milestone is coming up soon. Elif has already finished her task: the database works. But Mara isn't finished with the design yet.

Niklas is nervous, because he's responsible for the whole project. Elif says: “No problem, I'll help Mara. If we work together, we'll manage it by Friday.”

On Friday Mara sends the design. The tutor gives the team feedback: the app looks nice, but the login is too slow. Niklas fixes the bug at the weekend. In the last week they present their result to the whole course. Everyone claps, and the professor is very pleased.
questions: Why does the team have a video conference?
Who has already finished their task?
What does the tutor say about the app?
Why is Niklas nervous?

translate.tr: Elif has already finished her task.
wrong: Elif hasn't finished her task yet.
Mara has already finished her task.
Elif has already got her task.

translate.tr: The tutor gives the team feedback.
wrong: The team gives the tutor feedback.
The tutor asks the team for feedback.
The tutor gives the team a new task.

translate.tr: If we work together, we'll manage it.
wrong: If we work together, we won't manage it.
If we work separately, we'll manage it.
When we worked together, we managed it.

informatik-a21-09-cloud:0.text:
Felix is in his second semester at TU Wien. He takes lots of photos and stores all his university materials in the cloud. But today he gets a message: “Your storage space is almost full.”

Felix doesn't want to pay anything, but with his service extra storage space costs money. His friend Clara explains that TU Wien has its own cloud for all students. The data is in a data centre in Vienna and not in America.

Felix logs in with his university account. Then he installs the app on his laptop and on his phone. Now the app syncs his files automatically. Felix is pleased because he has access to his materials everywhere.
questions: Why does Felix get a message?
Where is the data of TU Wien's cloud?
Who tells Felix about the university's cloud?
What does the app do automatically now?

translate.tr: Unfortunately extra storage space costs money.
wrong: Luckily extra storage space is free.
Unfortunately an extra account costs money.

translate.tr: The data is in a data centre in Vienna.
wrong: The data is on a server in America.
The data was in a data centre in Vienna.
The data isn't in a data centre in Vienna.

translate.tr: He has access to his files everywhere.
wrong: He has access to his files nowhere.
She has access to her files everywhere.
He has access to his photos everywhere.

informatik-a21-09-cloud:1.text:
For a practical class Felix and Clara are writing a report together. Felix shares the folder in the cloud with Clara. She gets permission to edit the files. That way they can both work on the report at the same time.

In the evening Clara is on the train to Linz. There's no internet connection there, but she can keep writing offline. In Linz something goes wrong: Clara deletes the report by mistake.

Felix stays calm, because the cloud keeps old versions for a month. He can restore the file quickly, and after a minute the report is available again. Even so, he now makes a backup every Sunday. And because of data protection he's glad that the servers are in Vienna.

gloss.lang: for (einen Monat lang — for a month)

questions: What does Felix do with the folder?
Why does Clara write offline on the train?
How long does the cloud keep old versions?
What does Felix do every Sunday now?

translate.tr: They can both work on the report at the same time.
wrong: They can both work on the report in turns.
They both have to work on the report at the same time.
Nobody can work on the report.

translate.tr: Clara doesn't have permission for this file.
wrong: Clara has permission for this file.
Clara doesn't have a copy of this file.
Felix doesn't have permission for this file.

translate.tr: He can restore the file quickly.
wrong: He can delete the file quickly.
He can't restore the file quickly.
She can restore the file quickly.

informatik-a21-10-studium:0.text:
In October Viktor starts his first semester at TU Wien. He's from Graz and doesn't know the city well yet. His first lecture is called “Introduction to Programming”. The lecture hall is so full that some students are sitting on the floor.

Every lecture also has a practical class. There the students solve small problems on the computer. Viktor learns a new word: Lehrveranstaltung. At TU every lecture and every practical class is called that.

A student in her third semester explains to him that he has to register online for every course. He also has to register for the exam in January. “If you want to pass the exam, go to every practical class!” she says.
questions: Where is Viktor from?
Why are some students sitting on the floor?
What is a Lehrveranstaltung at TU?
What does Viktor have to do online?
